statement.p: Calculate the Riemann sum for f(x,y)=4 x - 8 y and domain \mathcal{D} in Figure 2 with two choices of sample points, \bullet and \circ.
Which do you think is a better approximation to the integral of f over \mathcal{D} ? Why?

static.solution:
\Delta x=\Delta y=1 and area \Delta A=1\cdot 1=1.
(\bf a\it) Sample points \bullet. There are six sample points that lie in the domain \mathcal{D}.
We compute the values of f( x,y )=4 x - 8 y at these points:
\begin{array}{l}f( 1,1 )=-4,\qquad\\ f( 2,1 )=0,\qquad\end{array}\begin{array}{l}f( 1,2 )=-12,\qquad\\ f( 2,2 )=-8,\qquad\end{array}\begin{array}{l}f( 1,3 )=-20,\\ f( 2,3 )=-16\end{array}
The Riemann sum is
{S}_{3,4}=( -4 - 12 - 20+0 - 8 - 16)\cdot 1=-60 (\bf b\it)Sample points \circ.
We compute the values of f( x,y )=4 x - 8 y at the eight sample points that lie in \mathcal{D} :
\begin{array}{l}f( 1.5,0.5 )=2,\qquad\\ f( 1.5,3.5 )=-22,\end{array}\qquad\begin{array}{l}f( 0.5,1.5 )=-10,\qquad\\ f( 1.5,1.5 )=-6,\qquad\\ f( 2.5,1.5 )=-2,\qquad\end{array}\begin{array}{l}f( 0.5,2.5 )=-18,\\ f( 1.5,2.5 )=-14,\\ f( 2.5,2.5 )=-10.\end{array} The corresponding Riemann sum is thus
{S}_{3,4}=(2 - 22 - 10 - 18 - 6 - 14 - 2 - 10 )\cdot 1=-80.
The approximation S_{3,4}(\circ) is the better approximation because it is calculated on more number of sample points. Also, its value is much closer to the actual value of the integral.
